title: Difference between MPS and RPO
description: Understand the essential differences between RPO and MSP, and why RPO is the preferred choice for many companies
contentHtml:
The world of talent acquisition is vast and understanding strategies of recruitment like RPO i.e., Recruitment Process Outsourcing and Managed Service Provider i.e., MSP is really important to master it. They play a vital role when it comes to hiring for organizations that want to optimize their staff management.

For all those seasoned HR professionals or those looking for innovative recruitment solutions, understanding the fine details of RPO and MSP is crucial. It helps in making informed decisions in the ever-evolving talent acquisition field.

We’ll discuss below the major difference between Recruitment Process Outsourcing and Managed Service Providers, their functions, what are their benefits, and the contributions of both in creating recruitment strategies.

RPO and MSP: Understanding In Details

If you are from the talent acquisition industry, it is crucial to dive deeply into Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) and Managed Service Providers (MSP). Let’s see what they are:

RPO services:

One can outsource the process of recruitment entirely to external experts.

MSP

Through MSP, one can outsource the contingent workforce management of an organization. 

Both RPO and MSP streamline the process of recruitment and hiring to ensure optimal management of the workforce. One can enhance recruitment efficiency through RPO Services Dubai by handing over the responsibilities of finding the right candidate, initial screening, and employee onboarding to people outside of the organization. It lets organizations focus on other areas that require attention while leveraging the benefits of expert and professional recruiters.

Through MSP, the management of the contingent workforce is outsourced, which addresses temporary and contract workers’ needs. It helps in creating a centralized approach to contingent labor management, including compliance, vendor management, tracking performances, etc.

That is why it is of utmost necessity for organizations that want cost-efficient recruitment solutions to understand the RPO and MSP. Both have distinctive benefits and opting for either of them totally depends on the organization’s needs and objectives.

If one wants to opt for RPO or MSP over traditional recruitment models, understanding their dynamics and strategic approach is important. Not only it will help in optimizing the workforce but also help in contributing to the organization’s success overall.

What Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) Is?

Recruitment Process Outsourcing in short RPO is a strategy to optimize and streamline the recruitment process for companies to restructure hiring. RPO recruiting enables companies to engage with external service providers (RPO providers) to manage and streamline various hiring aspects. This is the collaborative model that is based on outsourcing specific recruitment tasks or the process entirely to hiring experts in the talent acquisition industry.

The primary purpose of RPO is efficient and effective outsourcing of recruitment. Organization and RPO providers work collaboratively to understand hiring needs, organizational culture, and business objectives and goals. Through these services, aligning with the objectives of the clients and tailored solutions are provided.

Through RPO, one can avail of the following services:

  • Ideal candidate sourcing 
  • Profile screening, 
  • Interviewing 
  • Employee onboarding 

The use of advanced technology and innovative strategies for recruitment is involved in RPO recruiting. It helps in attracting and engaging top-tier talent.

Moreover, flexibility is another advantage of RPO recruiting that organizations enjoy. It helps them outsource specific tasks related to recruitment or go for full-fledged recruitment solutions. This allows them to limit their recruitment hustle according to the demand of the business. 

From saving the cost to managing the time efficiently, and accessing a diverse pool of talented individuals, RPO recruiting offers immense benefits as well.

What Managed Service Provider OR MSP Is?

MSP or Managed Service Provider plays a vital role in talent acquisition or recruitment. It is an inclusive recruitment approach that focuses on managing the contingent workforce and all the aspects related to it.

MSP recruitment lets companies partner with service providers externally to manage their contingent workforce including temporary, freelance, and contract workers efficiently. MSP providers are responsible for overviewing the lifecycle of the entire contingent workforce, from sourcing candidates to their onboarding and evaluating their performance.

The basic MSP recruitment goal is strategically and efficiently managing workforce solutions with flexibility. This is done by streamlining uniform processes, implementing tech-based solutions, and being compliant with relevant labor laws and regulations.

MSP providers tailor their services by collaborating with organizations and companies closely and getting brief on their specific needs for a contingent workforce. MSP recruitment is essential to enhance the control, visibility, and cost-effectiveness of contingent workers management.

Here are some of the key components on which MSP recruitment relies:

  • Vendor management
  • Talent pool optimization
  • Performance Analytics

MSP providers have lots of vendors on board to streamline procuring contingent talent. In addition, they do data analyses to provide workforce trend insights, ensure workers meet KPIs, and explore opportunities for cost optimization.

Why Companies Prefer RPO

RPO or Recruitment Process Outsourcing is a preferred choice for organizations now and there are various reasons for it. The purpose of seeking RPO is to enhance the strategies for talent acquisition. The RPO bypasses the traditional in-house recruitment methods and utilizes external experts for recruitment by outsourcing the entire process to them. Here are some reasons why RPO is popular among organizations these days:

Efficiency:

Efficiency is the primary attraction for organizations that seek RPO. As recruiting providers are experts in their field and can streamline the hiring and employment lifecycle like pros, they become a sigh of relief for companies. Organizations are maximizing their efficiency by handing over the staff sourcing and profile screening, conducting their interviews, and worker onboarding. This expedites the company’s hiring process which is really crucial in the competitive environment businesses are thriving today.

Cost Effectiveness:

Another reason why companies prefer RPO is the cost-effectiveness it brings. Outsourcing recruitment lets companies save time and eventually it reduces their recruitment cost. Companies with fluctuating hiring needs do this particularly as it lets them scale up or scale down without burdening themselves with recruitment expenses constantly.

Specialized Talent Acquisition

RPO service providers have a team that specializes in talent acquisition. Their skills with in-depth industry knowledge together can bring the best possible recruitment solutions for companies to the table. Their expertise sources top-tier relevant talent. They stay ahead of trends in the industry, and they use the latest recruitment technologies for employment that companies might find costly to use in-house.

Benefits of RPO

Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) is indeed an impactful and strategic recruitment solution for the talent sourcing and hiring needs of organizations. As we have discussed why RPO is preferred by the companies, let’s discuss some of the benefits that RPO offers to the organizations:

Scalability and Flexibility: 

If you need a recruitment approach that is flexible as well as scalable in the future, RPO provides the best solutions. Through RPO, companies can modify their employment capacity easily with changing business demands. RPO’s flexibility lets companies efficiently manage their efforts for recruitment while it is expanding or contracting.

Strategic Workforce Planning: 

RPO services provide strategic recruitment solutions with a planned workforce that aligns with the goals of the client’s organizations. They have a proactive approach that helps client organizations and companies build a pipeline full of talent to make it future-ready for clients.

High Quality Candidates: 

As RPO service providers have specialized strategies for recruitment, the quality of the hires is top-notch. Their screening process is advanced, their assessments are unmatchable, and their selection criteria for candidates match the company’s values and culture.

Technology Integration: 

As we have already discussed RPO services leverage the latest technology for recruitment. From candidate tracking systems to AI-based tools for candidate selection to using data analytics for performance evaluation; they integrate different technologies to enhance the recruitment process efficiency and effectiveness overall.

Key Differences Between RPO and MSP

The key difference is that MSPs manage the entire process, while RPO providers may provide specific services. An RPO, on the other hand, may only provide candidate screening or sourcing services, while an MSP would manage all aspects of contingent workforce.

If you want to manage talent acquisition by outsourcing it, there are two ways; Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) and Managed Service Provider (MSP). These approaches are different from each other and understanding them is crucial for organizations and companies who want to optimize their recruitment strategies. Let’s discuss their core difference below:

Service Scope

The service scope of RPO and MSP are different. Where RPO offers full-fledged recruitment services for all types of workers and staffing, MSP only focuses on the management of a contingent workforce. Here are the differences in service scope of RPO and MSP:

Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) service scope comprehensively and strategically deals with the nuances of talent acquisition and the tailored solutions are provided by learning the organizational goals. Whereas, MSP manages contractual, freelance, or contingent workforce management on the go:

Through RPO, social media and job boards are leveraged to source and attract talent followed by tough screening and comprehensive assessments. It ensures the progression and hiring of only top-notch and highly qualified candidates. From interviews to selections, and onboarding, RPO services handle it all. 

While MSP only source, recruit, onboard, and manages contingent workers who are hired or fired temporarily according to the organization’s demand.

Technology Integration

Both RPO and MSP integrate advanced technologies for recruitment. One of these includes Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) that help enhance overall efficiency and provide real-time insights. 

RPO recruiting also practices employment laws and ensures compliance with it. Whereas, MSPs often ignore them as the labor laws for freelancers and contingent workforce are different. RPOs do not manage after onboarding performances whereas, MSPs regularly analyze workforce performances through different tools to generate detailed reports performance. 

Strategically Focused

Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) is strategically focused on talent acquisition that aligns with the organization’s goals. It is mandatory for RPO service providers to comprehend clients’ recruitment objectives, their hiring challenges, and their staffing needs. It is the strategic approach that lets RPO help organizations with their success.

On the other hand, MSP focuses on recruiting and managing a contingent workforce only with limited scope of services.

Customized Recruitment Strategies

Through strategic RPO services, one can get customized recruitment tailored to their specific organizational needs. This involves targeted efforts of talent sourcing, initiatives for employer branding, and talent pooling. All the recruitment strategies of RPO are scalable, adaptable, and agile and can be customized with organizational demands.

On the other hand, MSP relies on the strategies of the client’s organization and provides their services accordingly.

Engagement Model

The engagement between the RPO service provider and the client’s organization is dynamic and contemporary. Contrary to the traditional recruitment approach, the RPO model is quite interactive and focuses on ongoing collaboration and communication between the client and the RPO service provider. 

Also, the RPO acts as an extension to the client’s internal HR and recruitment team that uses seamless integrated systems, and expertise to perform recruitment processes. Not only does it bring RPO providers and clients close, but also makes sure that the RPO service provider keeps in mind the goals, values, and objectives of the clients while hiring.

On the other hand, MSP is a managed service provider that only looks after the recruitment and management of a contingent workforce that does not necessarily have to follow the client’s organizational culture and values.

Consultancy Approach

The RPO approach is a recruitment consultancy that provides organizations with industry insights and then data-based recommendations according to their industry expertise. This collaboration extended beyond just recruitment drives and strategic planning for the workforce. RPO recruitment is always in contact with its clients to evaluate their talent needs in the future, communicate skill gaps, and implement dynamic workforce solutions suitable for organizational objectives.

Contrary to that, MSP focuses on just hiring and management of freelance and contractual workers and does not provide recommendations or suggestions regarding the company’s policies.

Cost Structure

Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) is financially viable and transparent. It has a flexible framework that is efficient and aligned well financially with the client’s organization. It has a streamlined cost structure that delivers value-driven results.

In the RPO cost structure, expenses are often structured based on the volume and complexity of hires, allowing clients to scale resources according to their hiring needs. This scalable approach ensures that organizations only pay for the services they require, making RPO a cost-effective solution compared to traditional recruiting methods.

Additionally, the cost structure in RPO is often characterized by a shift from fixed to variable costs. This means that as hiring demands fluctuate, the cost structure adapts accordingly, providing financial flexibility for organizations. By aligning costs with hiring volumes, RPO enables clients to optimize their recruitment budget and allocate resources strategically.

FAQs

1. What is the main difference between Recruitment Process Outsourcing (RPO) and a Managed Service Provider (MSP)?

RPO focuses on managing permanent hiring processes, while MSP oversees the procurement and management of contingent or temporary workers. In short, RPO hires employees; MSP manages contractors.

2. How does RPO help organizations improve their talent acquisition process?

RPO providers streamline recruitment using data-driven strategies, technology, and expert sourcing to attract top candidates faster and reduce hiring costs.

3. What are the key benefits of using an MSP for managing a contingent workforce?

MSPs centralize vendor management, ensure compliance, reduce workforce costs, and provide visibility into temporary staffing performance and spending.

4. When should a company choose RPO over MSP for its hiring needs?

 A company should choose RPO when it wants to improve or scale permanent hiring efforts. MSP is a better fit when managing large numbers of temporary or project-based workers.

5. Can RPO and MSP services be integrated to create a complete workforce management solution?

Yes. Many organizations combine RPO and MSP models to create a unified talent strategy that covers both permanent and contingent staffing under one system.
